audit.whatIsWrong: The chain that actually kills Aurora was never described, and the ultimate was described as something it is not. Hero's Entrance is called "a flight-in taunt" (mid), "taunt you right as your team engages" (wants.foe[1]) and a level-6 lane engage you "dash away from with E" (whys[3], spikes[1], wants.you[1]). Riot's R text: he designates an ALLY's position, shields all allies in the area, then smashes down and knocks up — no taunt anywhere in it. The taunt is Shield of Durand, and it only reaches 275. Meanwhile whys[5], spikes[3] and late all say Aurora's R lets her "phase around his taunt zone" — a taunt is applied to a champion, not a zone, and Aurora's R has no phasing in Riot's text.
audit.why: The real interaction is a two-part delivery: Justice Punch charges 650 and knocks up the first champion it meets, which is what puts you inside the 275 taunt. And a taunt is the one form of CC Aurora's whole kit cannot answer — being fast does not help when you are walking back toward him.
audit.corrected: Justice-Punch-into-taunt now stated explicitly with both ranges and the 11s cooldown; Hero's Entrance re-described as an ally-targeted, ally-shielding, map-crossing knock-up on a 180s cooldown; the phase-around-the-taunt claim removed.
sources: galio kit E text and range 650
galio kit W text and range 275
galio kit R text and range 4000/4750/5500

audit.whatIsWrong: Six content fields state Galio has no poke and no waveclear: whys[0] ("no real poke or wave clear before 6"), whys[6] ("Lacking real damage or lane pressure at any point"), spikes[0] ("almost no wave clear or poke"), early ("essentially no poke and mediocre wave clear", "can't punish your aggression with anything beyond basic autos") and mid ("his own damage is low").
audit.why: Winds of War is an 825-range spell that converges into a tornado dealing damage over time, on 11/10/9/8/7. That is both poke and waveclear, and it is only 75 range short of Aurora's Q. Telling the reader the lane is free is why a 51.86% matchup reads like a 60% one.
audit.corrected: Difficulty re-grounded: Aurora's edge is 75 range and his travel time, not an absence of tools. Every "he has nothing" claim replaced with the actual cooldown window.
sources: galio kit Q text, range 825, cooldown 11/10/9/8/7

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3].why claimed "three-spell spirit stacks proc your passive haste", breakdown.spikes said "Luden's makes the rotation half a bar", and spikes[0] told the reader to "punish his passive shield timing".
audit.why: Aurora's passive heals and grants no haste. "Half a bar" has no source. Galio's passive is Colossal Smash — every few seconds his next basic attack deals bonus magic damage in an area. It is not a shield; the brief flags it as the auto-reset burst tell.
audit.corrected: Spike text rebuilt on the real structure: full kit at 3, his 6 landing on the map rather than in lane.

audit.why: Justice Punch is 11/10/9/8/7 — 11 seconds at rank 1, not fifteen. Shield of Durand is 18s, Winds of War 11s, Hero's Entrance 180s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Concrete sequencing written in: step up only in the window after Justice Punch is spent, stated in winCon, cooldowns, ahead, loading, whys[2], spikes[0], early and wants.you[0].

edits.before: Galio has essentially no poke and mediocre wave clear before level 6, so pushing the wave hard with Q denies him easy farm and opens up roaming opportunities your kit is built for. He can't punish your aggression with anything beyond basic autos at this stage, so playing forward in lane is almost always correct. Just keep vision up for jungle ganks since he brings no pressure of his own to punish overextension otherwise.
edits.after: Galio does have poke: Winds of War is an 825-range tornado that deals damage over time on an 11-second cooldown, and it clears a wave as well as it chips you. Your edge is those 75 range and the travel time. Justice Punch steps him back, then charges 650 and knocks up the first champion it meets — that knock-up is what delivers Shield of Durand, which only taunts inside 275. The sequencing that matters: step up after the punch is spent, not before.

edits.before: At 6 he gains Hero's Entrance, a flight-in taunt that can set up a kill if it lands clean, but the cast time is long and telegraphed enough that dashing away with E well before he arrives denies the entire combo. He remains reliant on his team to follow up since his own damage is low, so soloing him in lane continues to be safe and profitable. Keep shoving to free yourself up for roams since his kit offers nothing to punish your rotations.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance is not a taunt and it is not really a lane spell. He designates an ALLY's position from over 4000 range, shields everyone standing there, then smashes down and knocks up whoever is near. At 180 seconds on rank 1 it is a map cooldown, so the level-6 change is that every fight on the map now has a fifth body in it. Track it. In lane the pattern does not change: he still needs Justice Punch to reach you, and Shield of Durand still only taunts inside 275.

edits.before: Your damage output stays well ahead of his through the late game since he's typically building tank items that add little offensive scaling, letting your poke and burst carry the lane advantage into fights. In teamfights, Between Worlds lets you phase around his taunt zone entirely, so you can ignore his engage and go straight for the backline he's trying to protect.
edits.after: Shield of Durand taunts everything within 275, and a taunt is not something you route around with mobility — once it lands, your leaps are irrelevant until it ends. Hero's Entrance also shields every ally in the landing zone, so a fight he joins starts with part of your burst absorbed. Enter with R from the flank and spend your rotation on a carry standing outside his reach.

notes: PACKET SUSPECTNAME IS A FALSE POSITIVE: "Time Hero's Entrance" in wants.foe[1] uses the correct R name. The real defect in that line was calling the ultimate a taunt — it is an ally-targeted landing that shields allies and knocks up; the taunt is Shield of Durand. CHART LEFT ALONE DELIBERATELY: all seven full phases[N].side read "Skill" while content win[] and the packet chart read "Aurora". At 51.86% over 1265 games "Skill" is arguably the better verdict on every row and "Aurora" the worse one, which is the opposite direction from the other matchups in this slice — so flipping either way would be me picking, not reading. I also do not know whether the content win[] field accepts the token "Skill" at all; every value I have seen in it is a champion name. See questionsForUser. UNVERIFIED AND NOT WRITTEN: whether tenacity, Cleanse or QSS shortens the Shield of Durand taunt (this is the single most useful thing a reader could know here and Riot's text does not contain it); whether Galio's W damage reduction while charging applies to Aurora's Q recast hit; and whether Aurora's W invisibility prevents Justice Punch from selecting her as the first champion it encounters. RANGE OF HERO'S ENTRANCE: the kit gives 4000/4750/5500. I wrote "over 4000" and "anywhere on the map" rather than calling it global, since it is not.
